# 1. What the current repository actually establishes

## 1.1 Review scope and limitations

This review read current repository metadata, selected implementation sections, the model card, learning mathematics, current plan status, corrected benchmark reports, confirmation findings, and actual GitHub Actions job results/logs. It did not execute local training or independently reproduce the saved experiments. A local clone attempt failed because this environment could not resolve GitHub; repository reads succeeded through the connected GitHub tool. Some original experiment artifacts are intentionally outside tracked Git files, so their reports are not equivalent to independently inspected raw observations.

Treat code inspection, CI observations, repository-reported results, external authors' results, and proposed experiments as separate evidence categories. Recheck HEAD at execution time and reconcile any intervening changes. [C1–C10]

## 1.2 Preserve completed work

The current repository is substantially beyond the earlier `8793c49` review. It includes explicit comparison tracks, matched frozen-feature heads, independent component-mode sleep, full-state snapshots, stable neuron identities/lineage, finite-update boundaries, role-aware evaluation, resource records, and bounded artifact/resume workflows. Do not rebuild these from scratch or re-open completed work merely because an older plan listed it as missing. [C2–C5]

Important current boundaries:

| Area | Current supported interpretation | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| NumPy models | Binary supervised learners; ordinary deep PC and circadian deep updates differ. | Use shallow parity controls now; resolve shared deeper mathematics before deeper mechanism attribution. |
| Torch models | Multiclass image heads, including matched heads on shared frozen ResNet features. | Useful starting point for external encoders and other heads. |
| Replay | NumPy retains labeled replay; the Torch circadian head currently has no sleep replay buffer/update. | Torch experience replay is real missing work, not assumed parity. |
| Sleep | Legacy, independently switched components, and disabled modes exist. | Extend component mode and preserve legacy reproduction. |
| Prediction | Held-out prediction is feedforward; label-conditioned latent relaxation happens in training. | Do not claim serving uses an iterative inference loop, or use training energy as a label-free novelty detector without defining a new observable. |
| Biological labels | Chemistry is an activity-derived numerical proxy; reward is supervised difficulty scaling. | Neither constitutes biological neurotransmitter dynamics or reinforcement learning. |
| Research status | No general CPC advantage has been established. | Market positioning remains a hypothesis. |

## 1.3 Current results change the earlier story

The corrected September 30 seven-seed hardest toy profile reports these mean balanced accuracies:

| Method | Mean balanced accuracy |
|---|---:|
| Backpropagation | 0.743265 |
| Ordinary predictive coding | 0.786122 |
| Circadian predictive coding | 0.768163 |

This is a descriptive reproduction of a previously tuned profile, not a clean causal comparison: deeper update rules, initialization, capacity, replay, and work are not all matched. Nevertheless, it reverses the earlier headline ranking between PC and CPC. In the moderate profile, the stronger bundled circadian policy gives the same mean balanced score as the baseline circadian policy despite additional splitting/sleep. Keep both findings visible. [C6]

The retained primary confirmation report has 105 available simultaneous intervals including zero, and eleven primary statements ineligible because their observed differences have zero variance. It leaves H1–H4 unresolved within that evidence. This is not equivalence, not proof that every mechanism fails, and not a reason to select favorable secondary endpoints. Repeated rendering or same-input replay of a report is not a new independent experiment. [C7]

## 1.4 Immediate engineering blocker

For commit `1820775`, CI run `37511207519` shows a successful Torch CPU job. The Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.14 general jobs fail type checking and skip the subsequent test step. The inspected 3.11 log reports eight errors in Windows-specific `ctypes`/`msvcrt` attribute typing across:

Repair platform boundaries and typings; do not globally suppress type errors or claim that the unexecuted general tests passed. Validate Linux and Windows behavior separately. [C8]

## 1.5 Prevent research administration from becoming the product

The tree metadata reports an approximately 1 MB existing development plan and a roughly 184 KB README. That is a navigation warning, not evidence that provenance is unnecessary. Introduce a compact active roadmap and claims register while preserving frozen records, historical task IDs, and source-pinned evidence. Do not casually edit files whose bytes are part of a retained scientific protocol. Any migration needs a compatibility/preservation check and an explicit new version. [C9]

# 2. Research review: what to borrow, what to test, and what not to assume

“State of the art” here means relevant frontier research and strong established controls, not a claim that every selected method is the universal current winner. Recent preprints and author-maintained implementations are labeled accordingly. Integration requires pinning a concrete version, reading its actual training code, and reproducing a small reference behavior before changing it.

## 2.1 Stable width/depth scaling for predictive coding — highest scientific priority

**Source:** Innocenti, Achour, and Bogacz, *On the Infinite Width and Depth Limits of Predictive Coding Networks*, ICML 2026. The paper derives stable parameterizations for linear PC networks and studies alignment empirically in nonlinear networks. Its equilibrium/width assumptions do not establish arbitrary finite-network equivalence with backpropagation. [S1]

**Application proposal:** implement a new, versioned deep PC formulation with an explicit scalar objective, verified local derivatives, and the paper's applicable parameterization. Compare standard fan-in initialization with the published prescription, including latent learning-rate/precision scaling. This is particularly relevant because the inspected NumPy initialization uses a fixed normal scale while the model can change width. Do not transplant a scaling rule into the legacy formulation without checking its assumptions. [C3,C4]

**Experiment:** widths 32/64/128/256 and depths 1/2/4 in small matched networks; log activation/residual/gradient norms, convergence, finite-update failures, training work, and held-out outcomes. These sizes are proposed pilot settings, not performance claims. Repeat after a structural event. Test that neutral circadian control reduces to the new PC reference.

**Decision:** scaling changes must improve stability or a measured task-cost tradeoff; merely aligning a diagnostic curve is insufficient. Read the full paper and exact reference implementation before claiming a faithful reproduction; the verified publication abstract alone does not specify all implementation constants.

## 2.2 Loss of plasticity — distinguish remembering from still being able to learn

**Sources:** Dohare and colleagues, *Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning* (Nature, 2024), with the authors' Continual Backprop implementation; later spectral-collapse work provides an additional diagnostic hypothesis. [S2,S3]

**Application proposal:** compare the current protective gate against selective renewal of mature low-utility units, residual adapters, and simple regularization. A mechanism can preserve old outputs while making new learning too slow. Add fresh-task learning probes, dead/saturated-unit fractions, feature effective rank, utility/age distributions, and bounded renewal controls. Spectral measurements are diagnostics, not automatic causal proof.

**Experiment:** same memory and capacity budget, recurring task streams, fixed small refresh budget; compare gate-only, renewal-only, gate+renewal, split-only, and unchanged reference. Do not combine all new tricks before measuring each. Preserve old-task performance and quantify recovery speed.

**Decision:** a controlled renewal mechanism is preferable to unconstrained growth when it produces the same retention/adaptation outcome with less memory or compute. This is a hypothesis to test, not an established property of CPC.

## 2.3 Replay and slow-target distillation — strong controls before exotic memory

**Source:** *Dark Experience for General Continual Learning: a Strong, Simple Baseline* (DER/DER++), an established rehearsal/distillation reference. [S4]

**Application proposal:** extend existing replay policies rather than duplicate them. Retain a bounded mix of recent examples and historical reservoir examples; add teacher logits/representations only when their semantics and storage cost are recorded. Port replay to Torch at the appropriate orchestration/kernel boundary. Compare with native backprop + replay and PC + replay at equal exposure.

**Technical requirements:** sample IDs, label-arrival times, deduplication, byte counts, deletion policy, context identity, encoder/head versions, and reference-logit schemas. A changed encoder invalidates naive feature replay; a changed class set invalidates naive logit comparison. Define migration, recomputation, or rejection rather than silently mixing coordinate systems.

**Decision:** test real replay before generative replay. A synthetic “dream” must not replace all genuine anchors or become its own unverified truth source.

## 2.4 Open-Jev and Contrastive Language Models — best first external-model integration

**Sources:** Zefan Cai's Open-Jev implementation/model packages and the Contrastive-LM team's CLM release. These are author-maintained systems with their own reported evaluations, not independently verified proof that CPC will improve them. [S5,S6]

**Terminology:** Open-Jev is not Open-JEPA. In this roadmap, CLM means **Contrastive Language Models**, because that is the directly related state/action decision system. **Context Language Models** and causal language modeling are separate optional tracks below.

Open-Jev packages use upstream Qwen weights plus LoRA, a scalar decision head, and calibration. CLM separates state/action embeddings and trains small heads with a contrastive objective. Both provide a useful entry point for changing decision tasks without initially retraining an entire foundation model. [S5,S6]

**Application proposal:** begin with cached embeddings and a small circadian-managed decision head. Keep the native supervised ranking/contrastive objective. Add matched replay, importance-aware update controls, optional bounded adapter growth, and safe promotion. Only later explore local PC updates for a small head under a separately named objective.

**Required controls:** candidate-order invariance where the task is permutation invariant; candidate-set size; action availability; probability calibration; abstention; request schema; cold/warm latency; encoder/head/cache versions. A ranker cannot choose a correct action absent from its candidate set. Measure candidate recall and ranking quality separately. Synthetic template variants from one source group must not straddle train/test.

**Important upstream caution:** Open-Jev explicitly distinguishes saved game-state decisions from live rollouts and reports weak/negative pilots. Preserve that distinction in our own demos rather than using a probability screenshot as evidence of an agent solving a game. [S5]

## 2.5 V-JEPA 2.1 — representations and action-conditioned prediction

**Sources:** official V-JEPA 2/2-AC/2.1 code and the March 2026 V-JEPA 2.1 paper. The updated recipe includes dense predictive supervision and intermediate-layer supervision. [S7]

**Application proposal:** use a pinned frozen video/image encoder, then train a small transition/predictor head and action head. Add action-conditioned latent prediction, episodic sequence replay, and sleep-time consolidation. Start with the smaller available encoder suitable for measured hardware; do not begin by reproducing internet-scale video pretraining.

**Required controls:** stop-gradient/teacher behavior, representation variance/collapse, temporally disjoint video splits, encoder-version stability, action units and time interval, closed-loop success. A label-conditioned PC training diagnostic is not the same objective as JEPA representation prediction.

**Decision:** first demonstrate improved adaptation of a downstream predictor or policy. A new full encoder/pretraining recipe is a separate expensive research hypothesis.

## 2.6 Dreamer-style world models — useful imagination requires real-world checks

**Sources:** DreamerV3 and the later *Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models* (Dreamer4) research direction. [S8,S9]

**Application proposal:** reproduce a small working world-model baseline, then independently adapt its latent dynamics, policy, or consolidation schedule. Use real transitions for model fitting and short imagined rollouts for candidate learning, with explicit horizon and imagined/real exposure accounting. DreamerV3 is a practical reference; do not assume an unofficial Dreamer4 repository faithfully reproduces the original system.

**Required controls:** multi-step prediction error, reward prediction, model exploitation, real-environment return, old-environment retention, imagined-rollout ratios, actor/critic/dynamics version identity. Accurate images or low latent loss do not establish a good policy.

**Decision:** use this lane after basic recurrent policy and environment integration works. Dreaming is a candidate training tool, not a source of guaranteed correct labels.

## 2.7 Test-time memory and learned adaptation — three distinct forms of “improvement while used”

**Sources:** Titans' learned test-time memory; SEAL's outer-loop optimization of adaptation directives; the September 2026 *Context Language Models* preprint. [S10,S11,S12]

Separate three mechanisms: (a) transient context/recurrent memory changes, (b) durable weight/adapter updates, and (c) learning the controller that chooses those updates. Updating a text memory file is not equivalent to learning model weights. SEAL's own setup highlights that adaptation rewards depend on the learner version; stale controller outcomes must not be treated as interchangeable. [S10–S12]

**Application proposal:** first implement deterministic bounded schedules and a stable deployed model with a shadow learner. Later train a small controller that selects among allowed replay budgets, learning-rate multipliers, gate settings, or sleep actions. The outer reward uses independently measured adaptation gains, retention, resource cost, and failures. Evaluation/safety gates and data permissions remain outside the controller's writable state.

**Decision:** learned control must beat a tuned fixed/heuristic schedule on new task streams after accounting for the controller's own training and evaluation cost. Self-generated justifications are not evidence of improvement.

## 2.8 Image generation — apply consolidation to adapters, not arbitrary neuron surgery

**Source:** official Diffusers LoRA training interfaces, together with replay/distillation principles above. This is an engineering transfer hypothesis, not a verified new continual-generation algorithm. [S13,S4]

**Application proposal:** keep a licensed pretrained diffusion or flow-matching backbone stable; adapt small modules using the model's native denoising/velocity objective. Compare sequential adapter tuning, replay, separate per-concept adapters, and a circadian-managed bounded adapter bank. Only consider shared-backbone updates after adapter-level evidence.

**Required controls:** old/new concept fidelity, composition, prompt adherence, diversity, held-out prompts/seeds, blind human comparison, memorization checks, rank/parameter/compute budgets, and checkpoints. FID-like estimates need adequate sample size and appropriate interpretation; small personalized sets need additional task-specific assessment. Generated data are marked synthetic and checked against genuine anchors.

## 2.9 Brain-inspired structure — separate practical circuits from biological reconstruction

**Sources:** Neural Circuit Policies (NCPs); a very recent September 30, 2026 preprint using a fixed 136-neuron biophysical C. elegans-derived core with learned interfaces; FlyWire adult brain reconstruction; and Loihi 2 connectome simulation research. [S14–S17]

NCPs provide a practical sparse recurrent sensorimotor starting point. The recent 136-neuron paper is especially aligned with the user's goal, but remains a fresh preprint: replicate its reference setup and competing controls before relying on its robustness claims. Its fixed core with learned adapters also differs from our proposed structurally adapting network. [S14,S15]

Use real connectomes as testable topology priors, not proof of transferred organism-level intelligence. Connectivity is only one part of a biological system; chosen neuron dynamics, sensory interfaces, body/environment coupling, and plasticity rules also define the simulation. Distinguish a functioning sensorimotor agent, a numerically verified circuit simulation, and a biological reconstruction. [S15–S17]

# 3. Mandatory instructions for the implementing agent

## 3.1 Living plan and evidence

Read `AGENTS.md`, this roadmap, the active portion of the existing development plan, relevant ADRs, and the latest work log before each session. Preserve existing instructions and unrelated working-tree changes.

**Update checkboxes as work proceeds, in the same logical change as the implementation or investigation. Do not wait until the entire roadmap is finished.**

Use stable IDs and these dispositions:

```markdown
- [x] R1.2 — Specify a coherent deep objective. — Coupled binary v1, working learner and135-case evidence in docs/coupled-predictive-coding.md; 2026-10-14.
- [x] R1.3 — Validate gradients and genuine neutral coupled CPC parity. — 171 combined cases and independent review; docs/coupled-neutral-control.md; 2026-10-14.
- [ ] R6.3 — Run encoder adapter study. — BLOCKED: missing approved model weights
- [x] R0.2 — Repair CI platform typing. — Evidence: commands, results, commit, CI link
```

Completion requires the task's acceptance checks and an evidence record. A negative or inconclusive experiment can complete an investigation; it cannot complete a separate claim that a feature improves performance. Reopen tasks invalidated by regressions. Deferred, canceled, or superseded work remains unchecked with the reason; do not count it as successful implementation.

Record exact commands, commit and dirty-state identity, dependencies, test pass/fail/skip outcomes, protocol/config/seed IDs, artifacts, measured resources, interpretation, limitations, and the next action. Keep large raw records outside the active checklist, using the repository's existing artifact conventions.

## 3.2 Adjustments are allowed and expected

Add, split, reorder, replace, or defer tasks when evidence justifies it. Record the original assumption, new evidence, rationale, affected dependencies, and revised acceptance criteria **before executing the changed scope**. Do not silently remove difficult work, tune on final tests, narrow the seed set, or loosen acceptance to manufacture progress.

This roadmap extends the earlier plan rather than erasing it. Cross-reference P2.6a, P6.12b, the deferred guard repair, and other still-open tasks after checking their current scope. New research gets new protocol IDs and new artifact locations; historical frozen settings and evidence remain untouched. Completing this plan does not automatically close older scoped tasks.

## 3.3 Limit concurrent work

Keep at most one active core-mechanism experiment and one active integration/demo implementation. A small read-only customer-discovery activity can proceed independently. Do not start all model families at once. Build only the abstraction needed by two concrete adapters; reject general frameworks that add complexity before a working example exists.

Each experiment has one primary question, a small predeclared set of comparisons, and explicit stop/continue conditions. Research progress is measured by changed understanding and task outcomes, not by number of generated reports.

## 3.4 Safety, privacy, and permissions

Default to local execution, synthetic/public licensed data, read-only external integrations, and simulated robotics. No new cloud spend, telemetry service, upload of private training examples, destructive action, public release, or live robot actuation without the required approval. Data access, action permissions, immutable instructions, emergency stops, and validation gates cannot be rewritten by a learning controller.

Do not train directly on unverified user/model outputs as ground truth. Preserve label provenance, consent, deletion controls, and delayed feedback. Quarantine poisoning/outlier events; rate-limit updates and bound drift. A “guard passed” result applies only to tested cases, not universal safety.

# 4. Proposed architecture

Keep `core` free of IO and use the existing inward dependency direction. Names below are proposed responsibilities, not claims that these files already exist. Reuse existing implementations where equivalent components are present.

```text
src/core/
  learning/              # versioned objectives, local/gradient update adapters
  plasticity/            # activity, importance, renewal, gated update policies
  memory/                # typed experience and pure retention selection
  consolidation/         # bounded replay/structure proposals and outcome types
  brain/                 # optional sparse recurrent circuits and dynamics
src/app/
  continual_runtime/     # orchestration through ports, immutable actor + learner
  studies/               # new versioned studies, existing runners remain usable
src/infra/
  encoders/              # pinned local pretrained model implementations
  environments/          # game and robotics adapters
  persistence/           # existing snapshot/artifact implementations or wrappers
src/adapters/
  demo/                  # dashboard/CLI/event presentation
```

Do not move all existing files into this tree as a prerequisite. Introduce small modules or ports adjacent to current code, then refactor only demonstrated duplication under tests.

### Minimal runtime contracts

Define a small learner port for `predict`, `learn`, `snapshot`, `restore`, and capability reporting. Objectives remain model-specific. Separate `ExperienceStore`, `ConsolidationPolicy`, `BudgetMonitor`, `PromotionGate`, and `EnvironmentPort`. The runtime should not inspect arbitrary private tensors to guess a model's semantics.

An experience record includes: event/sample ID; observation or local reference; optional next observation; action and candidate set; label or external reward; label-arrival time; episode/stream/context; model and behavior-policy version; preprocessing/encoder version; permissions; retention category; and optional teacher output/version. Do not require fake labels for self-supervised observations.

Use explicit clock domains: observations, completed learner updates, environment steps, episodes, wall time, consolidation attempts, and successful promotions. Do not inherit the toy runner's epoch meaning into a real-time control loop.

### Deployed behavior

```text
Observation → stable actor snapshot → allowed action/output
      │                  │
      └──── feedback/experience log ────┐
                                       ↓
                          bounded shadow learner
                                       ↓
                       replay / consolidation / checks
                                       ↓
                      candidate validation and promotion
                                       ↓
                           atomic actor version swap
```

This is an implementation design for continuous operation, not a promise that this assistant will run work asynchronously. The actor never observes partially mutated parameters or topology. Swapping models invalidates the appropriate caches and may require recurrent-state migration or an episode-boundary reset.

## R2 — Test plasticity, replay, and capacity mechanisms independently

**Dependencies:** G0; G1 for deep-PC mechanism claims. **Sources:** S2–S4.

- [ ] **R2.1 — Add learnability diagnostics.** Implement cheap active/dead/saturated fractions, activity/importance/age summaries, feature effective rank, and a reserved fresh-task probe. Acceptance: diagnostic overhead is measured, probe updates do not contaminate the deployed/benchmark learner, and retention is reported separately from ability to learn.
- [ ] **R2.2 — Add bounded selective renewal.** Implement a low-utility mature-unit refresh control with configurable maturity and replacement budgets. Acceptance: equal-capacity reference, safe state reset, reproducible unit IDs, and no arbitrary replacement of high-importance units.
- [ ] **R2.3 — Improve retention selection.** Extend the current memory implementation with explicit recent/reservoir budgets, deduplication, and per-example/byte accounting. Acceptance: old contexts remain represented under long streams without exceeding bounds; class/context balancing never accesses future labels.
- [ ] **R2.4 — Implement Torch rehearsal.** Add labeled/trajectory replay to the Torch route through reusable interfaces. Acceptance: independently switchable replay, declared side effects and clocks, equal-memory/equal-exposure BP controls, and snapshot/resume equivalence including buffer/RNG state.
- [ ] **R2.5 — Add slow-target distillation as an ablation.** Store or recompute teacher outputs with versioned semantics. Acceptance: evaluate replay alone versus replay+distillation, account for teacher storage/forward work, and detect stale encoders or incompatible output schemas.
- [ ] **R2.6 — Make capacity resource-constrained.** Compare split/prune, scheduled growth, equal-final-width reference, and bounded renewal; add cooldowns and measured utility criteria only when necessary. Acceptance: actual peak/average parameters, bytes, and work accompany outcomes; no inference of efficiency from small starting width.
- [ ] **R2.7 — Define a deployable shift signal.** Compare observable predictive uncertainty, feature drift, delayed supervised residuals, and persistence rules. Acceptance: synthetic stationary-noise and recurring-shift tests distinguish false alarms from useful triggers; no use of label-conditioned latent diagnostics before labels arrive.
- [ ] **R2.8 — Select a minimal successful bundle.** Run component removals around the best development configuration, then freeze a small confirmation family. Acceptance: either retain a measured advantage, simplify to a cheaper equivalent-within-prespecified-margin alternative, or record unresolved/negative evidence without inventing equivalence.

**Exit G2:** a small supported mechanism bundle—or an explicit finding that simpler controls remain preferable. Do not take every optional mechanism into later demos.

## R4 — Expand demos into actual closed-loop environments

**Dependencies:** G3 for adaptive deployment; simple environment fixtures may start after G0. **Sources:** S18,S19; baseline research S8,S14.

- [ ] **R4.1 — Define a common demo/evaluation contract.** A demo consumes actual recorded run events or runs a real environment, with a visible distinction. Acceptance: it displays method, seed, actor version, task sequence, train/evaluation state, and whether learning is active; no illustrative animation passes as measured evidence.
- [ ] **R4.2 — Build the recurring MiniGrid game.** Implement key/door navigation with a hidden cue and changed layouts/visuals in A→B→C→A streams. Begin with demonstrations, then a separately evaluated recurrent RL policy. Acceptance: complete live episodes, accumulated return/success, legal actions, old-room recall, and held-out layouts; one state snapshot is not a rollout.
- [ ] **R4.3 — Add game dynamics and delayed reward.** Change movement dynamics or action mapping in a second controlled stream; log real rewards and behavior-policy versions. Acceptance: equal environment-interaction budgets and repeated environment seeds, recurrent-state reset rules, and baselines trained under their own trajectories rather than claiming identical data under different policies.
- [ ] **R4.4 — Build robot imitation in simulation.** Use a small ManiSkill reach/push/pick task with state observations first, then frozen visual features. Acceptance: action units/bounds and episode termination validated; matched behavior-cloning or small policy baseline works before CPC adaptation is introduced.
- [ ] **R4.5 — Introduce robot domain drift and recurrence.** Vary camera pose/lighting, object properties, and bounded dynamics changes, then restore the original context. Acceptance: adaptation curves, old-task retention, constraint violations, real simulator return, and memory/compute accounting across a predeclared sequence.
- [ ] **R4.6 — Add a low-risk sensor/visual-drift demo.** Use a reproducible classifier stream with delayed corrections and recurring camera/sensor conditions. Acceptance: predict-before-update evaluation, calibration and false alarms, labels-to-recovery, and a simple scheduled-finetuning/replay baseline.
- [ ] **R4.7 — Build one shared inspector.** Show current environment, rolling old/new outcomes, actual topology/lineage, memory composition, sleep proposals/acceptance, and resource use. Acceptance: every metric resolves to a saved event; charts handle nulls/failures and do not hide inactive controls.
- [ ] **R4.8 — Package a reproducible comparison.** Provide a small CPU demo and optional GPU robot mode with clean setup and data licensing. Acceptance: replay of retained trajectories and a fresh-run path both work; live hardware is not enabled by default.

**Exit G4:** one complete game and one complete simulated robot task demonstrate the operational loop, whether or not CPC wins. A product-strength claim additionally requires measured advantage over strong matched controls.

## R6 — World models, vision-language-action, and image generation

**Dependencies:** G3 and a working relevant G4/G5 integration. **Sources:** S7–S9,S13. **Scope:** staged experiments, not simultaneous foundation-model pretraining.

- [ ] **R6.1 — Establish frozen V-JEPA features.** Load a pinned practical encoder and validate preprocessing/feature determinism and temporal splits. Acceptance: cache versioning and baseline downstream probe/dynamics scores; setup/feature extraction costs included.
- [ ] **R6.2 — Train an action-conditioned latent predictor.** Predict future representations from current state/history and actions, with declared time steps and teacher behavior. Acceptance: non-collapse checks, multi-step prediction, and action-sensitive counterfactual fixtures; no final-evaluation leakage.
- [ ] **R6.3 — Test circadian world-model adaptation.** Add replay and a bounded predictor/residual adapter under recurring environments. Acceptance: measured old/new prediction and closed-loop control outcomes; latent-loss improvement alone does not close the task-success claim.
- [ ] **R6.4 — Introduce short imagined rollouts.** Reproduce a small Dreamer-style reference before changing consolidation. Acceptance: all imagined work counted, real-rollout validation, bounded horizon, uncertainty/error checks, and explicit failures where the actor exploits model errors.
- [ ] **R6.5 — Probe a native VLA adapter only after robot baselines.** Audit a currently available official small VLA implementation, then test controlled adapter updates without replacing its native action representation/loss. Acceptance: verified checkpoint/protocol, policy-retention controls, and no assertion of whole-VLA PC training from a head-only change.
- [ ] **R6.6 — Establish sequential image-generation adaptation.** Use licensed/consented small concept sets and a native Diffusers-compatible LoRA recipe. Acceptance: frozen base, pinning, reproducible prompts/seeds, distinct training and held-out concept/prompt splits, and unchanged/per-concept/sequential baselines.
- [ ] **R6.7 — Add bounded consolidation to generative adapters.** Compare recent+historical replay, slow teacher, and adapter-bank selection; record total rank/parameters and update work. Acceptance: new-concept gain without unacceptable old-concept/compositional/diversity regressions under predeclared metrics and blind review; synthetic-only replay is not the sole retention evidence.
- [ ] **R6.8 — Select or close each integration lane.** Produce one report per model family, including negative results and total costs. Acceptance: expand only a lane with a reproducible benefit or a clearly valuable diagnostic result; archive unsuccessful mechanisms rather than carry them into every model.

**Exit G6:** evidence of transfer to at least one additional native-objective model family, or a well-scoped finding that the system adds no benefit there. Full backbone continual training remains conditional.

## R7 — Learn how to train while the system is being used

**Dependencies:** G3 plus reliable outcome signals from at least one G4/G5/G6 lane. **Sources:** S10–S12.

- [ ] **R7.1 — Define a finite adaptation action space.** Allowed choices include no update, bounded replay amount, learning-rate multiplier, gate setting, and sleep/renewal budget. Acceptance: hard envelopes cannot be changed by the controller; no arbitrary code generation or permission changes are executable.
- [ ] **R7.2 — Establish fixed and heuristic controllers.** Tune only on development streams; include no-learning, periodic, drift-triggered, and simple budget-aware references. Acceptance: controller overhead and opportunities-to-learn are recorded fairly.
- [ ] **R7.3 — Define the outer objective and chronology.** Use normalized new-task gain, old-task degradation, compute/memory, and violation costs with weights fixed before confirmation. Acceptance: labels/returns arrive causally; distinct controller-train, controller-validation, and sealed evaluation streams; no repeated tuning against one tiny guard set.
- [ ] **R7.4 — Train a small adaptation controller.** Start with a simple contextual selection/bandit or compact policy, using version-bound learner snapshots for counterfactual training trials. Acceptance: stale learner-version outcomes are detected; delayed effects and partial observability are acknowledged, and discarded candidate work is included in cost.
- [ ] **R7.5 — Test meta-generalization.** Evaluate on unseen streams, drift rates, noise levels, and recurrence schedules. Acceptance: improves the declared utility versus tuned heuristics, or reports a negative/uncertain result; no self-scored narrative substitutes for external outcomes.
- [ ] **R7.6 — Add validated data augmentation only if useful.** Candidate transformations/self-generated rehearsal carry source and validity checks. Acceptance: no transformed sample leaks evaluation content, no unverifiable target is treated as truth, and real-anchor retention is tested.
- [ ] **R7.7 — Run a long-duration deployment simulation.** Continuously serve while the controller updates the shadow learner under contention, delayed/noisy feedback, and poisoning fixtures. Acceptance: bounded growth, old/new utility, rejected promotions, tail latency, recovery, and a reproducible end-to-end ledger.

**Exit G7:** “improves its training while used” means externally measured, bounded, generalizing controller benefit—not recursive unrestricted self-modification.

## R8 — Define strengths and test market fit

**Dependencies:** discovery after G0; performance/pilot claims require G4/G5 evidence. **This section is a proposed business hypothesis, not market research establishing demand.**

- [ ] **R8.1 — Write a capability/claim matrix.** Separate working implementation, measured advantage, hypothesis, and unsupported claim. Acceptance: old optimistic benchmark descriptions are corrected; no “brain-like intelligence,” “never forgets,” or universal efficiency assertions.
- [ ] **R8.2 — Choose one initial customer problem.** Prioritize adaptive typed decision/routing heads or non-safety-critical visual/sensor drift; choose based on access to useful data and user pain. Acceptance: one specific workflow, feedback channel, buyer/operator, existing alternative, and measurable cost of current failures.
- [ ] **R8.3 — Conduct discovery interviews.** Proposed target: 10–15 relevant practitioners, without claiming that number already exists. Ask about retraining frequency, label delay, deployment constraints, failure tolerance, evaluation, and willingness to run a controlled pilot. Acceptance: sourced interview notes, disagreement and non-interest retained, no invented TAM.
- [ ] **R8.4 — Test against the actual operational alternative.** Include scheduled fine-tuning+replay, retrieval/calibration, and doing nothing when applicable. Acceptance: compare total labels, operator effort, GPU/CPU cost, latency, and downtime, not only a model benchmark.
- [ ] **R8.5 — Design two or three bounded partner pilots.** Establish consent, non-critical scope, success/stop criteria, data ownership, evaluation windows, and manual fallback before deployment. Acceptance: agreements and verified outcomes; prospective partners are not presented as customers.
- [ ] **R8.6 — Decide a product form.** Candidate: a local adaptation SDK with versioned model adapters and audit/promotion controls, with optional deployment/support offering. Acceptance: evidence supports integration value and economics; any commercial distribution gets current license/privacy review.
- [ ] **R8.7 — Update positioning from evidence.** If mechanisms do not outperform ordinary replay, position useful runtime/research tooling honestly or change the hypothesis. Acceptance: supported narrow claims, reproducible examples, documented limits, and explicit next customer/product decision.

**Exit G8:** a validated problem and comparative operational value—or an evidence-based pivot. A compelling demo alone is not product-market fit.

## R9 — Brain-inspired structure and scale

**Dependencies:** a minimal circuit prototype can begin after G0; adaptation needs G3/G4; scale escalation needs its own measured gates. **Sources:** S14–S17,S20.

- [ ] **R9.1 — Select a scientific target and fidelity tier.** Choose functional sensorimotor intelligence, connectome-inspired topology, or a particular biological circuit reconstruction. Acceptance: named organism/circuit when relevant, neuron model, temporal scale, observable behaviors, and non-claims; parameter count is not the target behavior.
- [ ] **R9.2 — Implement a sparse recurrent sensorimotor scaffold.** Separate sensory encoders, recurrent integrative units, action-selection/command units, and motor readouts; include feedback and persistent state. Acceptance: functioning closed-loop task; compare with matched random sparse, dense/recurrent, and NCP references.
- [ ] **R9.3 — Add distinct dynamics only where testable.** Experiment separately with timescales, excitatory/inhibitory sign constraints, bounded activity/homeostasis, and delayed connections. Acceptance: numerical stability, explicit biology-inspired versus measured biological parameters, and controlled ablations.
- [ ] **R9.4 — Integrate consolidation and temporal credit.** Add sequence replay, recurrent-state boundaries, slow memory, and native sequence training; investigate local eligibility-trace credit only under a separately specified rule. Acceptance: delayed-cue and delayed-reward learning, old-task retention, and fair comparison with truncated backpropagation through time.
- [ ] **R9.5 — Replicate a small biological-core reference.** Evaluate NCP first; separately attempt the recent 136-neuron core setup if code/model/data access and compute permit. Acceptance: exact retrieved resource versions, fixed-core versus learned-core distinction, randomized-topology/matched-dynamics controls, and no transfer of unverified preprint claims.
- [ ] **R9.6 — Build a versioned connectome importer.** Start with a defined worm circuit, then a selected FlyWire subcircuit. Acceptance: preserve IDs, direction, weights/counts, predicted versus observed annotations, missing edges, licenses, and trainable/fixed masks; validate simulation before structural rewiring.
- [ ] **R9.7 — Establish scaling and memory accounting.** Benchmark proposed tiers around 300, 3,000, 30,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000 abstract units with explicit sparse degree/dynamics. Acceptance: actual edges, bytes, steps/sec, checkpoint/trace overhead, task learning, and sparse-versus-dense backend costs; no auto-launch of infeasible tiers.
- [ ] **R9.8 — Define whole-circuit and large-scale behavior gates.** Test perturbation recovery, cue memory, recurrent environment retention, and transfer, not only spontaneous activity. Acceptance: replayable behavior and baseline comparisons; distinguish a dataset-sized graph from a biologically faithful whole-organism model.
- [ ] **R9.9 — Write a human-scale resource/research design.** Model synaptic state, sparse indices, activations, traces, communication, and checkpointing with explicit assumptions. Acceptance: identify which model dynamics and learning behavior would be preserved at scale; no claim that matching 86 billion units produces a human brain or consciousness.

**Exit G9:** a useful and scientifically interpretable sensorimotor architecture at the achieved scale, plus a justified next scaling experiment. Brain reconstruction is a continuing research direction, not a marketing requirement for the SDK.

# 6. Demo specifications and acceptance in greater detail

## 6.1 “A changing world that comes back” — game flagship

Build one small game well. Use a MiniGrid-like key/door task with partial observations and a cue that must be remembered. Present environments in a declared sequence, for example A (layout/appearance), B (changed appearance), C (changed bounded dynamics), A again, then D (held-out layout). Do not equate repeated exposure to the same training map with generalization to a new map. [S18]

Start with a fixed offline demonstration dataset to isolate supervised representation/policy learning. Then run a separate interactive study with a conventional recurrent policy and actual environment rewards. Different policies generate different observations; equal environment seeds do not make their training datasets identical. Report interaction budget, update budget, replay budget, evaluation episodes, and total simulation cost.

The viewer should show the real current rollout, retained-task success, elapsed interactions, memory composition, model version, true structural events, and current/peak parameters. Training rewards and no-learning evaluation returns must be visually distinct. Episodes that fail stay in the video/run report. Reuse the same trace schema for all methods.

## 6.2 “Learn the new workspace; remember the old one” — simulated robotics

First solve a simple reach/push/pick task with an ordinary imitation or small recurrent policy baseline. Then introduce appearance, camera, object, and modest dynamics variations one at a time. Separate perception drift from actuation/dynamics drift so a changed camera is not accidentally blamed on motor learning. Use both state observations and frozen image/video features as explicit tracks. [S19]

Use a stable low-level controller and bounded high-level outputs initially. Sleep can occur at episode boundaries or in a shadow learner while the actor uses a stable checkpoint. A successful rollout does not justify unsupervised live robot adaptation. Hardware transfer requires a separate review, emergency stop, action limits, and human-supervised acceptance.

## 6.3 “Useful changing decisions” — external-head and market-facing demo

A local tool-routing scenario exposes valid candidates and verifiable outcomes. Introduce a new tool, change a workflow rule, then return to an older domain. Distinguish recurring context from a globally superseded rule: old rules should be remembered when still applicable, not obeyed after explicit replacement.

Compare retrieval/linear scores, frozen Open-Jev/CLM, native fine-tuning, native fine-tuning+replay, and circadian-managed variants. Report top-choice accuracy, probability quality, abstention, missing-candidate rate, full workflow completion, cache hit/miss latency, and operator correction burden. All side effects remain sandboxed.

## 6.4 “A generator that learns several concepts” — later exploratory demo

Use a small series of consented/public-domain objects or styles; train A then B then C and evaluate each separately plus combinations. The critical question is whether adaptation preserves prior concepts and prompt flexibility at a bounded total parameter/rank budget. Keep seed/prompt grids fixed and show failures and diversity, not one hand-selected attractive image. Compare separate concept adapters as well as a shared consolidated adapter; added stored adapters count as capacity.

---

# 7. How to evaluate continual learning without hiding the hard parts

## 7.1 Protocol families

Maintain four explicit experiment categories:

**Offline supervised attribution:** matched examples, order, features, objective, initialization, allowed labels, and update exposure. Useful for isolating mechanisms.

**Causal streaming:** predict first, receive labels later, update only after arrival; held-out temporal windows and evaluation-only checkpoints. Report both initially deployed and adapted performance.

**Interactive control:** policies induce their own trajectories. Match environment-interaction and resource budgets, not nonexistent identical experience. Use paired environment seeds as variance control without claiming identical states.

**Meta-adaptation:** separate controller training/selection from held-out task streams. A controller cannot repeatedly query a fixed final suite to decide updates.

Test contamination sentinels at each boundary. Novelty, prioritization, replay selection, and early stopping must all obey the same label-arrival contract. Frequent promotion guards are part of development feedback; reserve a disjoint assessment route to detect guard overfitting.

## 7.2 Required comparison ladder

Start with no adaptation and a simple native learning baseline. Add native learning+replay before claiming benefit over a “standard network.” Compare PC-only, CPC-without-structure, and the full minimal bundle where objectives match. Include periodic versus adaptive consolidation, renewal versus growth, equal-capacity controls, and a retrospective wide reference clearly labeled as such.

Do not explode every optional factor into one huge factorial sweep. Use small staged development experiments, then predeclare the few primary contrasts justified by those results. Preserve complete old analyses; a new smaller confirmation family is a new protocol, not a retroactive redefinition of the previous 116-statement family.

## 7.3 Metrics and accounting

Report task success/accuracy or return, old-task degradation, recovery interactions/labels/updates, forward transfer where defined, recurrence recovery, calibration when meaningful, current/peak/average capacity, total replay bytes, total updates/latent steps, attempted and rejected consolidation, p50/p95 serving latency, and setup plus training plus evaluation cost.

Different losses are not directly comparable “energy efficiency.” Do not call low surrogate energy biological energy savings. Real power/energy claims require measured hardware energy with a stated method.

Use a proposed development pilot of three fixed seeds to estimate feasibility/variance, followed by a separate prospectively chosen confirmation sample based on effect-size and uncertainty requirements. Ten seeds can be a planning starting point, not a universal guarantee of statistical power. Report failed seeds, nonfinite results, and inactive mechanisms. Use paired contrasts when runs are genuinely paired; treat trajectories/users/tasks as the correct independent units rather than pretending every timestep is independent.

Define a minimum worthwhile improvement and acceptable retention/cost bounds before confirmation. “Not statistically significant” is not equivalence; equivalence requires its own prespecified margin/design. Negative and uncertain evidence should shorten the mechanism list, not trigger undisclosed retuning.

---

# 8. A realistic brain-size and brain-structure program

## 8.1 Structure first: functional roles, not three dense layers

A useful engineering decomposition is:

```text
Vision / audio / proprioception / symbolic observations
                         ↓
           specialized sensory encoders
                         ↕
       sparse recurrent integrative circuits
           ↕                         ↕
 fast episodic/context memory   slow consolidated memory
                         ↓
             action selection / commands
                         ↓
                motor/output circuits
                         ↓
              body / simulated environment
                         └── sensory feedback ──→
```

“Interneuron” is not simply a synonym for every hidden ANN unit, and “sensory→inter→motor” should not be presented as a faithful description of all human brain organization. In the functional engineering lane, label them sensory, integrative, and motor **roles**. In the biological lane, use the selected dataset's actual cell classes and preserve the distinction between observed and predicted annotations. [S14–S16]

Add recurrence, multiple time constants, bounded activity, sparse long-range links, and appropriately tested excitatory/inhibitory structure before pursuing raw scale. Standard dense/recurrent and randomized sparse networks are essential controls: otherwise any gain could come from recurrence or parameter count rather than biological topology.

## 8.2 Biological anchors and what they do not prove

The classic adult C. elegans hermaphrodite nervous system has 302 neurons; the recent robot-core preprint uses a 136-neuron sensorimotor subset, not the whole animal. FlyWire's 2024 adult female brain reconstruction contains 139,255 neurons and roughly 50 million reconstructed chemical synapses. These are useful concrete anatomical references, not claims that all synapses or dynamic parameters have been perfectly measured. [S15,S16]

A research demonstration has mapped a fly-scale connectome onto Loihi 2 hardware, with its own neuron model and hardware constraints. That motivates sparse/event-driven benchmarking, not a guarantee of the same gain on a consumer GPU or proof of complete biological behavior. [S17]

The widely used human estimate is approximately 86 billion neurons. It is a biological cell-count estimate, not a target parameter count for a foundation model and not a sufficient criterion for human-level function. [S20]

## 8.3 Scaling arithmetic — explicit illustrative assumptions

For a sparse abstract network:

`connections S = units N × average incoming degree k`

`weight bytes = S × bytes_per_weight`

A realistic runtime estimate adds sparse indices, neuron states, optimizer/momentum, plasticity/eligibility traces, saved trajectories, replay, and promotion snapshots. Costs also depend on temporal unrolling and connection activity.

Illustrative—not biological—budget with `k=1,000`:

| Abstract units | Connections | Weights at 2 bytes/connection | Example aggregate state at 16 bytes/connection |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 100,000 | 100 million | 0.2 GB | 1.6 GB |
| 1 million | 1 billion | 2 GB | 16 GB |
| 86 billion | 86 trillion | 172 TB | 1.376 PB |

Decimal units are used. These are arithmetic examples, not complete training-memory predictions, measured fan-in counts, or recommendations to launch those runs. Sparse-index width and recurrent/learning state can make the real requirement larger. Shared/factorized connectivity changes both compute and the scientific model; report that distinction.

Scale only after demonstrating the desired behavior and measuring the current tier. A million-unit agent with verified recurrence learning would be a meaningful engineering result; an 86-billion-unit allocation that has not learned a task would not establish a recreated brain.

---

# 9. Provisional strengths and market position

## What is supported now

The repository is a substantial experimental platform for studying plasticity control, structural adaptation, replay, evaluation boundaries, and reproducibility. The current reports do **not** establish general superiority, long-term autonomous learning in deployed robots, or product-market fit. [C2,C5–C7]

## What to try to prove next

Proposed positioning:

> A local, bounded adaptation layer that helps deployed models learn changing tasks while preserving required prior behavior and validating each promoted update.

The likely first package is an SDK around compact decision/perception adapters, not a claim to replace all neural-network training. This is an engineering/business hypothesis based on integration fit, not demonstrated demand.

| Candidate application | Proposed role in the roadmap | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| Typed tool/action routing | First external-model pilot | Better adaptation and calibration than native replay/retrieval at acceptable latency and operator effort. |
| Non-critical visual/sensor drift | First operational drift pilot | Fewer labels/retraining interventions with bounded old-condition regressions. |
| Simulated robotics | Scientific and technical showcase | Closed-loop retention/adaptation under controlled dynamics/perception shifts. |
| Game agents | Cheap recurrence/temporal-credit showcase | Learning and remembering across real episodes, not canned animations. |
| Generative personalization | Later adapter-consolidation experiment | Multi-concept retention, quality/diversity, and usable storage/compute economics. |
| Whole-brain reconstruction | Separate long-range research | Validated circuit dynamics/behavior, anatomy/data fidelity, and credible scaling measurements. |

Ask users what they would stop doing or paying for if the adaptation system worked. Evaluate integration and operation costs, not speculative market size. A native replay baseline that solves the problem more cheaply is a serious alternative; an honest result may favor selling reliable deployment tooling rather than a distinctive learning rule.

---

# 10. Milestone order and stop/continue decisions

| Milestone | Deliverable | Proceed when |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | Reconciled current state and repaired CI | Required checks execute successfully; remaining evidence gaps explicit. |
| M1 | Coherent deep-PC core and compact native runtime ports | Mathematics validated for PC claims; two concrete learners work through the ports. |
| M2 | Recurring game + sensor stream with strong controls | End-to-end operation reproducible and one mechanism question answered. |
| M3 | CLM/Open-Jev adaptation plus simulated robot baseline | External native losses and real closed-loop evaluation preserved. |
| M4 | Minimal supported mechanism bundle and customer problem | Gains or useful negative outcomes survive fresh evaluation; problem worth solving is evidenced. |
| M5 | One selected advanced model integration | A measured benefit justifies world-model or generative complexity. |
| M6 | Learned adaptation controller | Beats tuned simpler schedules after counting its cost on held-out streams. |
| M7 | Sparse sensorimotor research and measured scale ladder | Behavior and numerical fidelity justify each larger tier. |

Market interviews can begin early. A small circuit prototype can proceed without waiting for every model integration. Full-brain scaling, all-backbone PC training, unrestricted generative replay, and multiple expensive sweeps must not become prerequisites for the first useful result.

When a hypothesis is contradicted or unresolved, simplify, revise the hypothesis with evidence, or close that lane. Do not move to larger models merely to conceal a negative small-model result.

## Research and upstream implementations

- **S1 — Innocenti, Achour, Bogacz (ICML 2026), On the Infinite Width and Depth Limits of Predictive Coding Networks.** Peer-reviewed proceedings; publication abstract/metadata verified, exact algorithm implementation remains an execution prerequisite. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/innocenti26a.html
- **S2 — Dohare et al. (Nature 2024), Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning.** Peer-reviewed paper and primary author implementation. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07711-7 ; https://github.com/shibhansh/loss-of-plasticity
- **S3 — Spectral Collapse Drives Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning (2025 preprint).** Diagnostic research lead, not a universal causal rule. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22335
- **S4 — Buzzega et al. (2020), Dark Experience for General Continual Learning: a Strong, Simple Baseline.** Foundational rehearsal/distillation control, not labeled a new 2026 invention. https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07211
- **S5 — Open-Jev, author implementation and model packages.** Current trained-package/native-objective reference; reported outcomes and deployment limits are upstream claims. https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev ; https://huggingface.co/ZefanCai/Open-Jev-2B
- **S6 — Contrastive Language Models, official release.** State/action heads and native contrastive training reference; release performance claims not independently validated here. https://github.com/Contrastive-LM/CLM
- **S7 — V-JEPA 2.1: Unlocking Dense Features in Video Self-Supervised Learning (March 2026 preprint), plus official V-JEPA 2/2-AC/2.1 code.** https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14482 ; https://github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2
- **S8 — DreamerV3 / Mastering diverse control tasks through world models (Nature 2025) and official implementation.** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08744-2 ; https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3
- **S9 — Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models (2025 preprint, Dreamer4 direction).** Verify official implementation/checkpoint availability before reproduction claims. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24527
- **S10 — Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time (arXiv 2501.00663).** Learned neural memory research, distinct from durable global fine-tuning. https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663
- **S11 — Zweiger, Pari et al., Self-Adapting Language Models (SEAL, June 2025 preprint).** Full methods and limitations inspected. https://arxiv.org/html/2506.10943v1
- **S12 — Context Language Models (September 2026 preprint).** Different meaning of CLM from Contrastive Language Models. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37725v1
- **S13 — Official Diffusers LoRA documentation.** Engineering integration reference; exact base-model weights/data terms must be checked separately. https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/training/lora
- **S14 — Lechner et al., Neural Circuit Policies enabling auditable autonomy (Nature Machine Intelligence 2020) and official library/docs.** Sparse sensorimotor baseline, not a whole-brain replica. https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-020-00237-3 ; https://github.com/mlech26l/ncps ; https://ncps.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html
- **S15 — Qian et al., A Biophysically Detailed C. elegans Circuit as a Task-Agnostic Dynamical Core for Visually Robust Robot Manipulation (September 30, 2026 preprint).** Very recent, exploratory replication target; fixed 136-neuron core with learned interfaces. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.39322v1
- **S16 — Dorkenwald et al., Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain (Nature 2024).** Primary FlyWire reconstruction paper; use versioned data and annotation limitations. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07558-y
- **S17 — Wang et al., Neuromorphic Simulation of Drosophila Melanogaster Brain Connectome on Loihi 2 (2025 preprint).** Hardware-specific simulation evidence, not generic consumer-GPU speed or complete organism emulation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16792
- **S18 — Official MiniGrid documentation.** Configurable game/memory environments. https://minigrid.farama.org/
- **S19 — Official ManiSkill user guide.** Robotics simulation integration and benchmark tooling. https://maniskill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/index.html
- **S20 — Herculano-Houzel (2009), The human brain in numbers: a linearly scaled-up primate brain.** First-party synthesis of the author's group cell-count work; approximate biological counts, not ANN sizing rules. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/human-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/neuro.09.031.2009/full
